posts.text:
Is anyone else noticing a massive decline in their interest in sports?

NBA: Basically unwatchable. Nobody plays defense, everyone chucks threes, stars sit out games, and the first 82 games feel like a preseason. Pointless until the playoffs. 

NFL: Not even the sport we grew up loving. Horrific QB play, flags on every other play, defenders can barely touch anyone, commercials every 3 minutes, and somehow Josh Johnson is still starting games in 2026.

MLB: The Dodgers and Mets are treating baseball like a billionaire’s fantasy league. Hella goy slop. As refreshing as it was to see the Brewers winning, nobody outside of Wisconsin even cared.

College sports: Completely bastardized by NIL and the transfer portal. No loyalty, no identity, just 19-year-olds entering free agency every offseason and going to the highest bidder.

NHL: Probably the only major sport that hasn’t completely sold its soul, yet somehow has the worst marketing imaginable.

Everything feels overly corporate, watered down, and manufactured for gambling and social media engagement.

Are we getting older or is the golden age of American sports legitimately over?

MORE INFO: Israel has shared intelligence with the US indicating that Iran is developing chemical weapons for potential use against Israel and other countries in the region, Defense Minister Israel Katz told reporters. 

He also confirmed that the IDF and U.S. Central Command have prepared plans for a joint strike on Iran.

Chemical weapons. Katz said Iran sees chemical weapons as a potential “game-changer.” Israel has had the intelligence for some time, and its assessment is that Iran would use the weapons if it acquired them. Katz said Israel is determined to prevent that and must verify whether Iran has begun production.

How urgent is the threat? “If we thought this was already an imminent event, we would have acted,” Katz said.

The nuclear program. Katz said Iran is working to revive its nuclear program. In Israel’s assessment, a chemical arsenal could deter Israel and other countries from intervening, giving Tehran more room to advance its nuclear work.

Joint strike plans. Katz said plans for a joint operation are ready and the decision rests with President Trump. Israel prefers to coordinate with Washington but can strike independently if necessary. 

Katz said he, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the IDF chief of staff agree on that position.

Trump considered a strike before Israel’s elections. According to Katz, Netanyahu told Trump that Israel wanted to avoid a strike before the vote. Trump later called it off. 

Katz said Trump also weighs the views of regional partners, energy interests and the prospects for an agreement with Iran.

Iran could strike first. Katz acknowledged the risk of a preemptive Iranian attack and said Israel must be prepared to strike even under those circumstances.

Threats on U.S. soil. Katz accused Iran of actively working to assassinate Trump and harm other senior U.S. officials inside the United States.

Iran’s missile launchers. Katz linked the timing of any Israeli action to the difficulty of defending against Iranian fire. “The sooner we act to eliminate Iran’s missile-launch capabilities, the easier our defensive mission will be.”
